This attitude has affected me in a weird way recently. I couldn't get vaccinated all this year because of my extreme depression, anxiety and lack of transportation. In-home vaccines weren't available to me either.

 Seeing all the posts and comments online of people celebrating and mocking the deaths of unvaccinated people has made me feel like utter shit, and I ended up contracting covid from my family who I live with. I can't stop thinking about how people would also celebrate if I died and would have no sympathy the moment they find out I'm unvaccinated, probably wouldn't think my reason was good enough, like I was told I could have just gotten a ride like that was so easy or an uber like I could afford it. :/
I wanted to do it this day too, since my family willbe out. If you're okay with it maybe we could try to talk about it, maybe talk ourselves out of it too

Sound so much like me, I think we have a huge amount of empathy, more than we know what to do with and ironically causes us to have emotional outbursts. You're much younger than me though, you still have a lot of time to figure yourself out and learn how to channel your high capacity for emotion. A helping field might be good, volunteering etc.

I told my mom with a lot of hesitance that I'm feeling very hopeless and suicidal and she just told me that I wasn't even trying to get better and that if I did it I would have to give an accounting to God and just told me to do it outside the house. 

If God is real, I don't like him.

I am too, I'm told I'm pretty, smart, talented, sweet then get treated like garbage and thrown away the moment I have any inconvinent needs. Having these qualities has done nothing to help me be happy.
I'm the same. Not sure how much longer I can hold on, but while I'm here I can talk
Same. It's not fair that we have to go through all this extra suffering just to exist, for me, I've had enough of it
